publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Increasing energy demands, depleting fossil fuel reserves and exorbitant environment concerns, are forcing to look out for sustainable sources of energy. Solar energy in particular seems to be a highly appealing source of energy due to its huge accessibility throughout the world. However, variability of solar resource during the day-time and its unavailability during the night-time poses a major hindrance in its practical implementation, thus, demanding a stiff power management system to meet the load demand. This paper, elaborates the various strategical operational modes of isolated solar PV system interconnected with the battery storage system. The proposed strategy is capable of drawing power from the grid under energy deficiency conditions. Further, a look out into the 2.205 kW solar PV plant setup along with its simulation results (implemented on MATLAB 2015a platform) for varying solar source and corresponding load conditions are depicted in this paper.

articleTitle: Fractionalization of microgrid protection system through detection of zero sequence component of fault current
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The fault current at a particular node in microgrid system varies depending upon its grid connected and islanded mode of operations. In this scenario microgrid the function of microgrid central protection unit becomes challenging to maintain its simplicity and reliability during protection coordination. To make protection system more reliable and to minimize complexity and dependency of central adaptive protection, fractionalization of microgrid protection is proposed in this paper showing detection of only load side faults independently based on zero sequence current components. The proposed algorithm is verified in a Simulink model of a three phase AC microgrid and results are found acceptable.

articleTitle: An approach to locate tcsc optimally for congestion management in deregulated electricity market
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Congestion mitigation is one of the major problem faced by the transmission system operator in deregulated electricity market. In this paper, a congestion management approach based on optimal placement of thyristor controlled series capacitor (TCSC) in deregulated environment has been proposed. The most critical line having highest probability of occurrence of congestion is investigated. The optimal location for TCSC placement to mitigate congestion is found based on probability of occurrence of congestion in a transmission line. The performance of proposed technique is tested on IEEE 14-bus system.

articleTitle: Mitigation of subsynchronous resonance in DFIG based wind farms using fuzzy controllers
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: DFIG based wind farm with Type III wind turbines are the most popular choice of wind power generation industry. Mostly, these wind farms are connected to load centers by series compensated long transmission lines. Series compensated lines offer cost effective way to evacuate large power from these wind farms. But these wind farms connected through series compensated lines may be affected by Sub Synchronous Resonance (SSR). Induction generator effect is the predominant cause of SSR in series compensated transmission lines or feeders as suggested by earlier researchers. Fuzzy logic control offers an effective way to mitigate the effect of SSR. In this paper application of fuzzy controllers instead of PI controllers in partially rated converter has been proposed to damp out SSR oscillations. First fuzzy controller parameters like number of membership functions and shape of membership functions have been studied for effectiveness of fuzzy controller for SSR control. Then fuzzy controllers for RSC, GSC and DC Link Voltage Controller have been studied and compared for their effectiveness to mitigate SSR phenomena.

articleTitle: Genetic algorithm based optimal placement of phasor measurement units for harmonic source identification
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Owing to the continuous growth of nonlinear loads and penetration of distributed generation (DG) plants in the power system, the harmonics are increasing at an alarming rate. The harmonics generated at one location can affect the performance of other components because of the interconnected nature of power system and even affecting the performance of harmonic generating sources. Therefore, it is important to locate non linear loads for placing the harmonic mitigation devices. In this paper, the locations of harmonic sources are identified by the direction of power flow. The required harmonic current injection data is obtained by the phasor measurement units (PMUs). The placement of PMUs is costly and needs communication system at every substation. The optimal placement of PMUs is carried out using genetic algorithm (GA) and effectiveness of the method is studied on IEEE 69-bus system.

articleTitle: Survey on authentication and encryption techniquesfor smart grid communication
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Smart grid has emerged as efficient power delivery management system integrated with communication and information technologies. Smart Grid has capability to interact and manage the bidirectional communication between both the utilities and customers to monitor the energy usage. Nevertheless, increased interconnection and integration increased the complexity and cyber-attacks in the smart grid. In this paper, to secure the bidirectional communication various authorization and authentication schemes are studied. Due to the limited memory and to reduce the overload of authentication with electricity information on the communication line, some lightweight authentication and encryption techniques should be used. It has been found these lightweight schemes has provided security against various attacks. Also, key evolution and management of key provides data privacy for smart grid communication.

articleTitle: Solar PV based single stage cascaded nine level converter for grid interfaced systems
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper shows solar photovoltaic (PV) array fed to cascaded H-bridge nine level converter system where maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is achieved by the incremental conductance (INC) control algorithm. To have appropriate solution and utilization of PV modules and to maximize the solar energy extraction, the viable control and modulation are instigated. Here, the control is realized using the modulation compensation by the use of phase disposition pulse width modulation (PDPWM) technique. The design is carried out for a 5 kW system and the performance is studied in steady state and dynamic conditions. Simulations are made by using MATLAB/Simulink and the performance is validated under IEEE-519 standard.

articleTitle: Modified bridgeless landsman PFC converter for LED driver
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a modified bridgeless Landsman converter-fed power factor correction (PFC) for light emitting diode (LED) driver. The application is targeted for high brightness (HB) projection applications with brightness control of high brightness red-green-blue (HB-RGB) LEDs. The pulse width modulation (PWM) technique is used for current control to achieve effective brightness control of LED driver without compromising the efficiency. The modified BL- Landsman PFC converter is used to feed a dual flyback DC-DC converter which supplies power to the forced LED cooling unit and the LED lighting module with a galvanic isolation. The brightness control of LED is performed by synchronous-buck converter with current modulation. The proposed PFC based modified BL- Landsman converter design is based on discontinuous conduction mode of output inductor current for high power factor (PF). A hardware prototype of the LED driver is verified experimentally. The proposed LED driver performance evaluation at full and light load conditions is good for universal AC mains (90V-265V). The power quality parameters measured with calibrated instruments are within the acceptable limits of standard IEC 61000-3-2 Class C for lighting systems.

articleTitle: Design of a novel non-isolated boost converter for renewable energy system
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a new single switched non-isolated boost converter which can be implemented with modular solar PV panel. The operational principle is analyzed in CCM and DCM modes. The suitability of proposed scheme is well demonstrated through simulation results using PSIM 9.1.1 with a practicality of input voltage of 24 V. Output voltage ranges from 300 V to 350 V which makes it suitable to get single phase AC at 220-230 Volt r.m.s. Simulation is designed based on 75 Watt converter rating.

articleTitle: Simultaneous charging and discharging integrating EV for V2G and G2V
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Synchronization of EV to distribution grid is gaining attention as the vehicle will coordinate to distribution grid ensuring good power quality. Reduce the charging time of EV is one of the key goals in making user-friendly environment for electric vehicles. In this context, fast DC charging gives an interesting opportunity. This paper develops a Simulink model of synchronized charging and discharging of EV to distribution grid and for V2G and G2V applications, two types of converter schemes are also discussed. For making EV battery charging, the Simulink model comprises of dq frame converter control which consists of DC-DC. With this work, charging of vehicle will be fast and due to discharging of EV battery to grid, owner of vehicle will get the revenue so that overall charging price of vehicle will be reduced. Also, Two types of DC-AC converter scheme for V2G and G2V applications to find out best one on the basis of current THD analysis, prosperity of synchronization and charging-discharging control which is shown using curves of load current, source(grid) current and inverter current. Different aspects of EV's integration to grid are evaluated and better converter scheme is used in charging of EV and the results are shown.

articleTitle: A HTF based higher order adaptive control of single stage three phase grid integrated SPV system
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a hyperbolic tangent function (HTF) based higher order adaptive control algorithm with a perturb & observe (P&O) MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracking) for a three phase grid connected single stage SPV (Solar Photovoltaic) system with DSTATCOM (Distribution Static Synchronous Compensator) capabilities. The variable learning based HTF reduces the mean square error in the system, thereby improving the response of the system. This algorithm is easily implemented with simple mathematical formulations and calculations. The system is tested under various abnormal conditions such as load unbalancing, variable solar insolation etc. and test results have demonstrated the fast response of the control algorithm. The distortion levels of voltage/current are found within limits as defined in an IEEE-519 standard while feeding active power to grid and connected loads.

articleTitle: Behavior of fault current in microgrid systems
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: With the integration of DGs to utility side, drastic changes in fault current occurs across the system at different locations in a microgrid. In this paper different types of faults in microgrid system are investigated through simulation using Simulink-MatLab. The impacts of inverter interfaced DGs on fault current and importance of adaptive protection issues for islanded and utility microgrid are studied in this paper. Nature of fault currents has been observed at several locations in sample microgrid system through simulation.

articleTitle: Reliability evaluation of radial distribution system using analytical and time sequential techniques
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper describes, the basic distribution system reliability evaluation techniques using analytical and time sequential simulation techniques. It explains application of these methods to bus 2 of RBTS systems for reliability evaluation by calculating the basic system and load point reliability indices. Using generation of random numbers, determination of failed load point and probability distributions of the element parameters are presented. It also brings out the variation in the expected customer outage costs using analytical techniques. It includes the effect of the application of the repair duration distributions on the expected customer outage cost and the probability distributions of the reliability indices.

articleTitle: Market bid optimization of a hybrid solar-wind system using CAES
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The prominent limitation with solar or wind energy system is its intermittent nature. It is important to utilize these resources with proper storage devices. Nowadays, compressed air energy storage is the upcoming storage technology for large scale storage purposes. Whenever there is bidding for market, the generator has to ensure constant power availability. Taking into consideration the variability of the solar-wind energy generators, the optimization needs to be done for the charging and discharging of storage devices and provide a constant power output. In this paper, an optimization problem has been solved for a constant power output. A hybrid solar-wind energy system with CAES as storage has been considered and the utilization with solar and wind energy system has been maximized.

articleTitle: Power factor correction in modified sepic converter fed switched reluctance motor drive
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a dual output PFC converter for switched reluctance motor (SRM) drive. Here, a modified SEPIC converter is proposed for wide range of speed control and to achieve power factor correction at AC mains. To regulate the DC link voltage, a single voltage sensor is used which output is used to drive the midpoint converter fed SRM. The switching frequency of the converter is considered at 20 kHz to reduce the overall size of the converter. It also presents the overall design and performance of the proposed converter fed SRM drive. The input current THD (Total Harmonic Distortion) is brought down below 5% as per the IEC 6100-3-2 standard.

articleTitle: Performance of doubly fed machines influenced to electrical perturbation in pumped storage plant - a comparative electromechanical analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Enhancing the reliability of pumped storage hydroelectric system is mandatory for building the stable network. This paper experimentally analyses the electrical and mechanical effects of voltage unbalance on doubly fed synchronous (fixed speed) machine and doubly fed asynchronous (variable speed) machine operating under motoring mode. The input electrical quantities such as stator current, rotor current, input power and losses are analyzed under normal and abnormal conditions. As well, the three-directional vibration of both the machines are analyzed under normal and abnormal operating conditions. The practical importance of this comparative analysis is for developing the robust system with the countermeasures for avoiding voltage collapse.

articleTitle: Analysis of induction motor drive using SPRS based on GTO/IGBT buck-boost chopper topologies
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Slip power recovery scheme (SPRS) is a method of speed control of wound rotor induction motor (WRIM) in which some amount of rotor recovered power is feedback to main supply instead of wasting it in the rotor resistance. The various types of chopper topologies utilized for SPRS are buck, boost, and buck-boost chopper and type of semiconductor technology employed for switching devices i.e. Silicon controlled rectifier (SCR), gate turned off thyristor (GTO), metal-oxide semiconductor field effect transistor (MOSFET), insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT). This paper presents the analysis of induction motor drive employing SPRS based on GTO/IGBT buck-boost chopper and IGBT based pulse width modulated voltage source inverter. The analysis of various performances of induction motor drive has been carried out using two chopper topologies i.e. GTO and IGBT. The simulink/MATLAB toolbox has been used to develop the model of WRIM using GTO/IGBT chopper and PWM VSI. The effect of duty cycle on stator current, rotor current, speed, electromagnetic torque, DC link current, supply current, source reactive power, supply power factor, and THD have been investigated. The simulation results have shown that the chopper topology utilizing IGBT has superior performances compared to GTO.

articleTitle: Energy management system for local energy market in microgrid consisting fuel cell
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Energy Management System (EMS) is capable of finding the best solution to fulfill the demand of consumers completely, continuously and quickly. This paper evaluates the energy management system of a microgrid consisting fuel cell in day ahead market (DAM). EMS is used to obtain power profile of all generating sources and load for each trading interval. Local Energy Market(LEM) concept have been used to develop an algorithm for finding the Market Clearing Price(MCP) for Single Sided Auction(SSA) market and Double Sided Auction(DSA) market. The system used in this paper consists of PV (solar panel), WT (wind turbine), MT (microturbine), EWH (dump load), consumer load and Fuel cell (used as an energy storage device). Fuel cell is also modeled using various equations. Results demonstrate the difference between total cost for SSA and DSA market model.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of different optimization technique: Harmonic minimization in multilevel inverter
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a new optimization technique known as Hybrid Newton Raphson method to solve non linear transcendental equations that has multiple solutions. This technique is a combination of genetic algorithm and newton raphson method. This method effectively works and minimizes the dominant lower order of harmonics from the output voltage waveform of 11-level multilevel inverter and controls the magnitude of fundamental component of output voltage. It has been shown that proposed method gives better result as compared to the genetic algorithm. Theoretical results are verified with the simulation of 11- level cascaded H-bridge multilevel inverter with equal dc sources.

articleTitle: Optimal placement of distributed generator for maximun load allowability and reduced losses mitigating congestion of transmission system
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: With fast technological development in the field of electrical, electronics and software technologies the usage of electrical power is escalating at a faster rate, stressing the generation and transmission system. In order to have continuous supply, Distributed Generators (DG) are positioned at distribution systems meeting growing energy demands. DG increases the economic efficiency in addition to peak shaving. DG also has lower rates of greenhouse emissions and high energy security with optimum penetration and location. In this paper, optimum location of DG has been determined using two main factors viz. critical loading parameter and benefit index. Benefit index comprises of Voltage Profile Improvement Index (VPII) and Line Loss Reduction Index (LLRI).DG location has a crucial role in reduction of transmission and distribution losses, avoidance of up gradation of transmission and distributed infrastructure along with support, relieving distributed network congestion and providing ancillary services.

articleTitle: Designing and simulation of standalone micro grid for rural area using renewable energy resources
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents an integration of renewable energy resources for electrification of a village - Lumshnong, Meghalaya. The advantage of renewable energy is that they are easily available and are eco-friendly. In remote areas where grid connection is not viable at least a small portion of the load demand can be met by using resources naturally available there. First, the graphical information and climate has been analyzed. Secondly, the data of the household and community load of the village has been estimated. The optimum usage of energy has been figured out to provide electricity to the village using HOMER software. The paper includes MATLAB Simulink for the simulation of load analysis. The uniqueness of the paper is highlighted by providing the optimum and most cost efficient combination of the renewable energy resources.

articleTitle: A software approach for the prediction of efficiency of three phase induction motor at optimize iron losses
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This research article describe the prediction of best performance of three phase induction motor at optimized iron losses by using two different rotor cages of copper and aluminum at room temperature to maximum working temperature of the motor up to 70° C. The target is to compare the efficiency of the motor by using different combination of stator and rotor design (Discussed in Table-1), and to calculate the variables dimensions of this combination in terms of sensitivity analysis under the condition of above said temperature. With the help of mathematical equations of three phase induction motor a program is prepared on the MAT LAB by using GUI tool. The output of this program is put in the targeted input value of JMAG express for performance calculations of three phase, 11Kw squirrel cage induction motor. Genetic Algorithm (GA) is used as an inbuilt tool for optimization techniques and calculations of sensitivity analysis are completed by using correlation matrix.

articleTitle: A stationary reference frame based simple control for single stage SPV fed water pumping system using PMSM drive
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The fundamental objective of this paper is to deliver a simple, robust and economical solution for the solar water pumping. The topology employed for single stage SPV (solar photovoltaic) array fed water pumping includes a SPV array, 3-phase VSI (Voltage Source Inverter), PMSM (Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor) and the pump. As the SPV array converts the energy of the photon falling on its surface into electrical energy. It acts as a source of electrical energy. Whereas and the PMSM converts the electrical power to mechanical, acts as sink for electrical energy. VSI is used between SPV array and PMSM for the purpose of power processing so that the motor would get the power in its required form. PMSM is controlled using stationary reference frame control. The INC (Incremental Conductance) method is employed to enhance and to optimize the power output from SPV array. This method is one of the various MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracking) techniques available and gives a good response under fluctuating insolation conditions. This system is modelled using MATLAB/ Simulink and the system performance is visualized under constant and changing irradiation levels.

articleTitle: An accurate electrical model for atmospheric pressure DBD plasma in air with experimental validation
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: DBD (Dielectric Barrier Discharge) Plasma is generated with two or more electrodes separated through some dielectric material in plasma generating gas medium. DBD is essentially a capacitive coupled discharge and therefore, it essentially has capacitive component in the model. In this paper, a new electrical model for roller DBD plasma in air is presented that emphasizes the importance of stray inductance of mesh electrodes in the generation of steamer free plasma. Due to this stray inductance and capacitor in the circuit, the voltage and current oscillations of a few MHz are generated. These oscillations are damped out through plasma resistance of the model. The stray inductance, air gap capacitance and plasma resistance form a tank circuit that gets pulsating energy with a frequency of 10 to 100 kHz. In each pulse, the voltage and current oscillations are damped out in 8 to 10 micro seconds through plasma resistance only and hence, no external resistor is required for controlling the plasma discharge current. The damping of oscillations also ensures the plasma to be streamer free. This model also emphasizes on the generation of large current oscillations across the plasma that is highly unusual in the conventional DBD model. The simulation of this model in MATLAB simulink and its experimental results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Unaddressed threat to power grid infrastructure: Electromagnetic pulse
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Detonation of a nuclear weapon at high altitude, produces high magnitude Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP which will cover the extensive geographic region within the line of sight of detonation. This high magnitude EMP when interact with sensitive electronics network, has the competence to produce extensive and long eternal disruption and destruction to the critical power infrastructures like power grids that is sufficient to underpin the fabric of an economy. A single EMP attack seriously degrade or shut down a large part of the electric power grid in the geographic area of EMP exposure effectively instantaneously. In this paper, impact of EMP on power grid has been critically highlighted and an effort of understanding about the interaction of EMP with electrical power infrastructure has been made. Moreover, EMP as a threat to national security has been underlined and techniques of mitigations are also recommended.

articleTitle: A comparative analysis on WPT system using various power transfer methodologies and core configurations
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Recent days, the demand for wireless power transfer (WPT) system is highly growing since it is more convenient, reliable and safer solution for electric vehicle (EV) consumers. Static and dynamic power transfer systems are the two opted appreciable wireless charging techniques for user friendly EVs. In static and dynamic charging systems, low power transfer efficiency (ηp) between transmitter and receiver coils is the principle challenge in existing issues of wireless charging system. The paper mainly focuses on improvement of power transfer efficiency in the system. The analyses presented in this paper are tested for distinct face to face distances of the coils to observe the effect of reluctance on power transfer efficiency. Here two kinds of coil structures have been adopted and are tested with various core configurations to find the suitable combination for the enhancement of power transfer efficiency. The paper presents a comparative analysis on performance characteristics of WPT system using inductive coupled and magnetic resonance coupled (MRC) power transfer techniques. In MRC system, various compensation topologies are used to find the efficient topology which enhances the better impedance matching in the system. Further, the analysis on effect of aluminum shielding is alsoreported.

articleTitle: Optimal operation of single-winding self-excited induction generator for single-phase power generation
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, the optimum operation of single winding single phase self-excited induction generator has been investigated with series and shunt capacitor configurations. The optimum capacitors values for different configurations are obtained using the genetic algorithm for optimum voltage regulation. The optimization is carried out under MATLAB where fsolve is used to find the magnetizing reactance and generated frequency for optimum capacitances and given prime mover speed. With such optimal values of capacitors, the steady state performance of single winding self-excited induction generator found satisfactory and similar to two winding self-excited induction generator.

articleTitle: A novel fifth-order higher bucking converter
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, a fifth-order buck converter facilitating higher bucking operation is proposed. This topology has a step down gain which ideally varies between 0 and 1 for respective minimum and maximum duties of operation. In order to justify the effectiveness of this topology, a steady-state analysis has been carried out and design equations for converter circuit parameters have been obtained. A state-space model has also been formulated based on two switching circuits and an open-loop simulation studies have been carried out in PSIM simulator to verify its steady-state behaviour.

articleTitle: Pine needle biomass a potential energy source for himalayan region
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The Indian Himalayan region covering an area about five lakh km sq. about 16.2% of India's total geographical area. Most of the Himalayan region like Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh covers with tall, evergreen, pine trees have leaves in needle shape. During the dry months every year, dry pine needle fall from the trees and cover the forest floor, which destroy the fertile top layer and also lead to uncontrolled frequent forest fires. Due to wide spread availability of pine needles in the Himalayan region, it can be used for energy generation application, like electricity production through gasification for immediate local consumption and the national grid. Using pine needle for electricity generation will not only save the environment, by preventing forest fires, but also contribute to the energy demands and energy security. In this paper, the general context for the technical feasibility, potential of pine needle for electricity gasification and the availability of pine needle was studied including social and environmental factors.

articleTitle: Fuzzy logic controller based grid integrated PV system with multi level inverter
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A detailed modeling of fuzzy logic based three phase multilevel inverter with separate DC source for grid connected photovoltaic (PV) system in MATLAB is presented in this paper. The photovoltaic systems utilizes two conversion stages i.e. a boost converter for tracking the maximum power point and inverter as an interfacing unit. DC link voltage is controlled by fuzzy logic controller and switching signals for inverter are generated through unit current vector and triangular sampling controller method and thus it synchronizes the grid voltage and current in order to maintain unity power factor operation. Simulation results are presented to validate components models and control schemes.

articleTitle: Power flow control with cascaded transformer multilevel converter integrated with energy storage
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents the real and reactive power flow control with cascaded multilevel converter (CMC) in the grid. A distribution static compensator (DSTATCOM) is connected at the point of common coupling (PCC) supported from CMC via cascaded transformers. Instantaneous symmetrical component scheme is used to generate the reference current for the compensator. In multilevel inverter the ramp comparison current control using phase displaced multi-carrier pulse width modulated scheme is used for injecting the current. The battery is connected through bidirectional dc-dc converter to provide support for plugin hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) charging station. An optimized algorithm has been implemented to control the real and reactive power at the PCC and supply the required power to the charging station through a bidirectional dc-dc converter. To verify the proposed control strategy the simulation studies are carried out using PSCAD/EMTDC software.

articleTitle: Zero-Voltage zero-current switching scheme for high boost-up ratio converter
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper a zero-voltage, zero-current high boosting converter using an auxiliary soft-switching network is presented. The high boost ratio is realized by an interleaved boost converter with charge-pump on the load side. Due to the parallel structure of the converter, the auxiliary soft-switching network is capable of providing both zero-voltage and zero-current transitions to the main switches. Moreover, the soft-switching network provides zero current turn-OFF of the main diodes and does not impose any extra stresses on the devices. The converter can operate at a constant frequency of operation with pulse width modulated control. A 12 to 48 V, 100 W circuit, operating at a frequency of 50 kHz has been experimentally validated to verify the soft transitions, turn-ON and turn-OFF of the main switches and zero current turn-OFF of the main diodes.

articleTitle: A case study: Still water electrical generation: Evaluation of hybrid power generation efficiency of cascade hydropower plants with climate change impacts on reservoir based hydropower generation and demand challenges in water sector
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Effective utilization of scarce water resources has presented a significant challenge to respond to respond to the needs created by rapid economic growth in India and worldwide. In principle India's hydropower potential is impressive due to rugged mountain terrain from which snow and rain fed rivers produce significant amount of seasonal water flow. Demand for hydropower is increasing worldwide for generating pollution free electricity. Owing to this natural hydrological processes, In the context of growing impacts of climate change on water bodies and hydrologic cycle, study on prospects of reservoir based hydrologic cycles, study on prospects of reservoir based hydropower in India and worldwide are highly desirable. Storing water in reservoir is one of the globally recommended options to tackle climate change impacts on hydrologic cycle. In this case, the reservoir based hydropower that accumulates water during rainy season and produces electricity throughout the year, is one among the best options to address the current problem of seasonal power shortage is an old option and not of much help in green power generation with insignificant amount of seasonal water flow. Cascade hydropower plants inside Pipe or in Parabola canal in terms of power generation is evaluated on the basis of precise simulation-optimization technique using CFD Analysis. This research provides a solid quantitative-based methodology to assess the operation efficiency of cascade hydropower plants constructed in limited area and using a parabola canal design, and more importantly, proposes potential methods that could improve the operation efficiency of cascade hydropower plants using this new concept.

Author Keywords: Cascading series of reservoirs on parabola canal operation
potential power generation in still water
flow based power generation inside Pipe with Cascading series of turbines

articleTitle: An adaptive third order digital filter based technique of single stage 3P4W SPV system
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a single stage 3P4W (Three Phase Four Wire) SPV (Solar Photovoltaic) by using an adaptive third order digital filter based control technique. The proposed 3P4W SPV system has two main sections. The first section is used to obtain peak power from the SPV array by using an INC (Incremental Conductance) based control technique. Whereas, in second section, an adaptive third order digital control technique is used for neutral current suppression, harmonics mitigation, load balancing and power factor correction. Unlike the conventional control techniques, the proposed technique does not require any decoupled control, integral, phase estimation section and coordinate transformation. Therefore, computation complexity and calculation per steps are reduced. The experimental result are demonstrated to verify that the proposed control technique can mitigate the harmonics current and load neutral current under nonlinear loads and also provides good dynamic performance under various operating conditions.

Author Keywords: an adaptive third order digital filter based control technique

articleTitle: Neuro fuzzy based indirect vector control doubly fed induction generator
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Doubly Fed Induction Generator is especially used as wind power generators. An Indirect vector control is used better dynamic performance of DFIG. But the performance of closed loop control is largely influenced by the type of speed and current controllers used. Usually, proportional-integral (PI) based current controllers are used due its simplicity. But these PI controllers suffer from tuning problem. To overcome the problem, this paper presents Adaptive Neuro-fuzzy based speed controller for indirect vector controlled VSI fed doubly fed induction generator to minimize the torque ripple. The proposed ANFIS controller significantly reduces the torque ripple compared to that of conventional PI controllers without using any filter. The performance of the indirect vector controlled induction motor drive has been simulated at different operating conditions using the ANFIS controller and the obtained results are compared with PI controller. Additionally in the implemented SVM algorithm, the switching times proportional to the instantaneous values of the reference phase voltages. It eliminates the need the calculation of sector and angle information unlike conventional SVM method.

articleTitle: Controllers design for hybrid micro grid, a comparing study
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents modelling of a hybrid micro grid, consisting of two DG such as photovoltaic cell and a fuel cell. The micro grid comprises DGs, nonlinear loads, storage devices and operates either inter connected or isolated mode from the main distribution grid. Here for the voltage source inverter (VSI) based micro grid the controllers are designed, using various control strategies such as PQ and Fuzzy controllers. Here PQ controller and Mamdani fuzzy control are designed to restore the system during various disturbance conditions like grid connected mode, islanding mode and heavy load switching. The two control techniques have been tested and simulated using MATLAB/SIMULINK package and their results are compared.

articleTitle: Implementation of quadrilateral relay for three zone protection of transmission line
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The quadrilateral relayhas been implemented at the generating end of a 5 bus system in Simulink. The three phase voltage and current signals have been sampled for different faults with varying distance, fault resistance and inception angle. These sampled and rationalized signals are transferred to microcontroller for implementation of quadrilateral relay. The DC offset has been filtered from the current signal using full cycle window. The fundamental component of voltage and current signals has been extracted using FFT algorithm full cycle window. The fault resistance (R) and reactance (X) have been calculated using sine and cosine coefficients of voltages and currents for LG and LL faults. These values of R and X have been used for implementation of three zone protection scheme of transmission line. The effect of arc resistance and power swing on the quadrilateral relay has also been studied. The impedance seen by the relay has been calculated for location of the fault after its classification.

articleTitle: Power factor corrected BL-modular converter based SMPS for arc welding applications
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a modular configuration of a three-phase power factor corrected (PFC) arc welding power supply (AWPS) using bridgeless (BL) isolated Cuk converter. Discontinuous inductor current mode operation (DICM) of Cuk converter enables this AWPS to attain unity power factor (PF) inherently at the utility interface. In the proposed BL converter, the diode bridge rectifier (DBR) at the input side is completely eliminated thus reducing the conduction losses. The proposed modular converter configuration provides several meritorious features like single-stage power conversion by using devices with comparatively lower power ratings, ease of power expandability, etc. Moreover, quick dynamic response to load variations and inherent short-circuit current limit lead to excellent weld quality. The behavior of the power supply is examined concerning input PF, supply current harmonic content as well as output voltage and current regulation. Its behavior is investigated to verify its effectiveness for arc welding applications.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of quantum unitary gates in presence of noise in the field of quantum communication
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents the performance analysis of unitary quantum gate in presence of noise, using the time dependent Schrödinger dynamics of system Hamiltonian. The perturbed Hamiltonian is expressed as the sum of unperturbed Hamiltonian and perturbation of any real valued controllable function. The basic idea is to maintain the unitarity for corresponding time evolutionary system after time T and it is achieved after solving the time-dependent Schrodinger equation along with Dyson series expansion. This work presents the behaviour of time evolutionary process of quantum system, first without noise and then in the presence of noise. The aim of this paper is to provide a simple mathematical approach for realizing the approximate unitary quantum gates when noise is having its appearance in corresponding quantum control field.

articleTitle: Profit earned by GENCOs from unscheduled interchanges
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Electricity markets of many countries, which are in developing phase, are facing problems like frequency fluctuations, generation deficiency and their performance is very sensitive to small disturbances. Operation of such power system is a challenging task and innovative strategies are required to get rid of these problems. Power utilities of India have introduced new tariff mechanism, Availability Based Tariff (ABT), to overcome these problems of power system. ABT has a component linked to the frequency of power system known as Unscheduled Interchange (UI) charge. This new mechanism has brought significant changes in operating strategies of power system. The Unscheduled Interchange (UI) charge is an important component of ABT mechanism which has been included to regulate frequency of power system. To understand the benefit from unscheduled interchanges a power system having four generators of different GENCOs is simulated in MATLAB SIMULINK and profit earned by each GENCO following UI rates and according changing their power schedules is evaluated. All the generator models are simulated in Matlab Simulink.

articleTitle: Analyzing power transferred physically over committed usage by adding series compensation using birds' intelligence
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The power transferred physically over already committed usage is important and needs to be accurately calculated. It will promote the commercial transaction opportunities when power transmitted is above the actually committed, however, the commercial transactions will be limited if it is lower. This can be accurately predicted using available transfer capability calculation. The birds' intelligence technique is proposed to accurately calculate the transfer capability for the thyristor controlled series compensated (TCSC) system and the obtained results are compared and validated with the results obtained using conventional techniques on the six-bus system.

articleTitle: Model reduction of LTI systems using spectral projection with application to power systems
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The present work deals with the problem of order reduction using balanced singular perturbation approximation. Direct truncation and singular perturbation approximation are two fully compatible order reduction method for a linear time invariant system, and both methods yield a stable, minimal, and internally balanced reduced model with the equal error bound. This paper presents an efficient technique for computation of full rank approximation of Gramians by matrix sign function which allow to reduce models of order up to O(10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>). Model reduction of unstable system can be performed by system decomposition via block diagonalization of the sign function method. Further, the effectiveness of the algorithm is validated with application to power system.

articleTitle: A review on techniques for placement of distributed generators
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The integration of Distributed Generation (DG) in distribution system is growing very fast since last decade. The integration of DG is beneficial if DG of optimal size is placed at optimal site. The optimal placement of DG (OPDG) helps the distribution system planners to conquer maximum benefits of DG integration. Many techniques are reported in literature to solve OPDG problem. This paper presents the state of art review of the OPDG techniques.

articleTitle: A hybrid filter as an integral component of HSES for establishing smart cities
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Rising penetration of renewable energy based distributed generation system in the utility grid has raised serious concerns towards poor power quality problem. The problem gets further alleviated if the electric system is intended to operate under smart gird philosophy. Management of bidirectional power flow with the utility and smart loads is a tricky aspect. The paper presents an innovative solution to overcome the power quality problem in a smart grid environment where major generation of power is catered through hybrid sustainable energy system (HSES). Methodologies for integrating a hybrid active filter (HAF) and its control aspect is demonstrated. Case study highlighting the role of HAF in a hybridized renewable energy regime demonstrates the effectiveness of proposed solution.

articleTitle: An EV battery charger with power factor corrected bridgeless zeta converter topology
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: An EV (Electric Vehicle) is becoming more popular these days in transport sector due to its environment friendly operation as well as availability at reduced cost. The battery charging process is the prominent matter of concern in an EV because of power quality issues in the input current drawn by the charger. These issues are generated mainly because of the nonlinear nature of the diode bridge rectifier (DBR), used at the input side of the charger for AC-DC conversion. The abovementioned problem is minimized if the DBR is eliminated at the input, along with added advantage of reduced conduction loss in the circuit. Therefore, this paper proposes a bridgeless isolated PFC (Power Factor Corrected) based EV battery charger with a zeta converter topology which uses constant current/constant voltage mode control for the battery charging. The proposed bridgeless converter is designed to follow IEC-61000-3-2 PQ (Power Quality) standard i.e. it draws a perfect sinusoidal input current with low THD from AC mains with all the advantages of zeta converter topology like low output ripple voltage, a non-inverted output, stable output response and effective control. Therefore, the overall efficiency is improved for the proposed front end bridgeless converter. MATLAB/Simulink based model is developed which is used to verify the performance of the proposed bridgeless zeta converter at rated condition as well as fluctuations in the supply voltage. The converter' performance is evaluated with a 48V 100Ah lead acid battery being used in EV which exhibit an improved power quality indices for the source current that is well within international PQ limits.

articleTitle: A comparative study of control strategies for the flyback SMPS
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The paper tremendously comprises the revision of different category of control techniques of the flyback converters operating under discontinuous conduction mode (DCM). The document of the art not only envisages the comprehensive control techniques due to wide range of load and input voltage variations but also suitably demonstrate the different methodologies of the controllers to improve performance of the flyback switched mode power supply (SMPS). The informative and important statements of the control techniques are fantastically devoted to the flyback converter as inclusive and indispensible comparisons and basses under the various operating controls and remarkable mode of the operations of the converters.

articleTitle: Economic load dispatch of wind thermal integrated system using dragonfly algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Majority of electricity produced across world is from thermal power plants and they causes environmental pollution. With the increased awareness regarding environmental protection several countries has allotted share for electricity generation from wind power. As wind power is a clean energy, wind thermal integrated systems reduce emission. Wind integrated system are considered in this study along with valve point effect. The economic dispatch problem becomes highly nonlinear while considering valve point effect. The situation becomes more stringent when intermittent wind power is integrated with thermal system. In this paper Dragonfly Algorithm is implemented to solve the economic load dispatch problem with valve point effect. This dispatch model includes both Thermal and Wind farm. The stochastic nature of wind is modeled using weibull distribution function and over estimation/under estimation cost is analyzed using closed integral function. The model is tested on a modified IEEE-30 bus system comprising 6 thermal generating units and one wind farm. The performance of Dragonfly Algorithm is validated by comparing with other metaheuristic algorithm on the test systems. The proposed dispatch model can minimize the generating cost and enhance the renewable power consumption capacity. The MATLAB software 2010b has been used to simulate the model. The simulation demonstrates that Dragonfly Algorithm is capable of finding global optimum solution and is free from local optima problem as compare to other traditional and metaheuristic optimization techniques.

articleTitle: Sitting and sizing of capacitors in distribution system using adaptive quantum inspired evolutionary algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The deficits of power at load centers are mainly occurring due to the losses in transmission and distribution network. The structure of distribution network is complex and large. It may produce high power losses and poor voltage regulation. In present power sector scenario the reduction of power losses in the distribution system can significantly improve the reliability and overall efficiency of power network. Therefore, several methods have been implemented for reduction of power losses in the distribution system. The power losses are reduced by optimization of conductor size, load management of distribution transformers, voltage correction etc. One such method of reduction of power losses is placement of capacitors. Reduced power tariff with improved quality of power is the benefit gained by the consumer. Sizing and placement of capacitors in distribution system is a difficult combinatorial optimization problem. Efficient deterministic techniques are not available, hence metaheuristic are used for finding optimal solution. In this paper an adaptive quantum inspired evolutionary algorithm (AQiEA) is used for finding the optimal sizing and location of capacitance. For test case studies two networks, 33 bus system and 69 bus system are considered and the results are compared with the other algorithms in the literature. Experimental results are compared with some 'State of Art' existing algorithms, which show that the proposed technique outperforms some of the existing techniques.

articleTitle: A review on prognosis and diagnosis of transformer oil quality using intelligent techniques based on dissolved gas analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The prognosis and diagnosis of evaluating the oil quality for high voltage electrical power transformers for maintenance is ever-demanding. The durability of transformers function is somewhat driven by the excellence of its insulation which degrades with time because of changes in temperature and content of moisture. The accurate diagnoses of faults in early stages and the efficient assessment of oil quality using an intelligent program is the key challenges for protection of transformers from incipient faults that occur during operation to avoid economic losses. The dissolved gases analysis in oil is a predictable approach in the fault diagnosis and evaluating the quality of insulating oil in transformers. In the recent applications of artificial intelligence include Fuzzy Inference, Neural Networks, Genetic Algorithm, State Space and Search, and other Expert Systems has the ability to meet DGA standards. This paper represents review of most of the methods used to diagnose faults and assessment of insulating oil for transformers through the dissolved gases analysis DGA. Further the future work provides alternate techniques for fault diagnosis and bio oil based insulations for transformer protection.

articleTitle: Unit commitment scheduling by employing artificial neural network based load forecasting
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Unit commitment scheduling of generating units in power system depends on the predicted load demand, load trend, availability of units, generating capability of generators, minimum up/down time of the units and their initial status. Previous know-how of various utility companies, differing commitment schedules of generators can result in vast difference in total operating cost acquired. Accurate hourly and daily load forecasting holds up an important purpose in appropriate scheduling of generators. This work represents a method to carry out unit commitment by employing the medium-term load forecasting based results attained from neural network learning. Both structure learning and parameter learning processes are utilised to train the neural network. The input data is composed of historical weather sensitive data such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, time variables such as hour of the day, day type (weekday, weekend, and holiday), month of the year and hourly load demand data. For structure learning, a relative analysis on the multi-layer feed forward networks and recurrent networks has been performed. The performance of the different network topologies is judged on the basis of mean square error and training time. Parameter learning is conducted on the optimally preferred network using supervised learning and the results acquired are reported.

articleTitle: The choice of controllers for the flyback converters as real time optimizations
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The paper attracts on the smart selection criteria of the controllers operating in the closed loop systems for the wider range of disturbances, load and input voltage variations of the flyback converters. In order to achieve outstanding regulations of the converters, the linear and nonlinear dynamic behaviors are tremendously productive for the robust stability and reliability to compensate for irregular sluggishness in the system. The smart recommendations and robust tuning of the controllers ensures to improve the dynamic response of the system to disturbances. The crooked disturbances of the prototype are proficiently minimized from the power converter system by the best possible settings and tracking of the performance parameters of the controller.

articleTitle: Estimation of optimal li-ion battery parameters considering c-rate, SOC and temperature
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: To improve both the operating performance and cycle life of batteries in battery electric vehicles requires a battery model that can influence fidelity behavior of the battery under different conditions. Hence, two commonly used equivalent circuit battery models (first-order and second-order RC) are tested using GA, PSO, and ASMO optimization techniques. The paper describes the estimation of parameters of battery model at various temperatures for the Li-ion battery. To diagnostic estimation, battery terminal voltage characteristic curve estimation accuracy during charging and discharging scenarios used for comparing. Feasibility of various optimization techniques evaluated by the accuracy of predicted model and the rate of convergence in predicting the model parameters. For performance investigation, optimization techniques are compared in terms of performances index such as mean, standard deviations, worst and best fitness functions values. The lower mean fitness value and standard deviation of the ASMO prove its durability as well as reliability in the battery parameter estimation scenario. Further, the low computational requirements signify the robustness of the algorithm, thus making ASMO as prime choice for the task of battery parameter estimation. Also the second order RC model proved out to be more robust as for all scenarios and the performance of optimization techniques improved by use of this model.

articleTitle: A smart solar power cultivation using the flyback converter & multi-level inverter
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The paper attracts on the substantial introduction of the smart solar powered battery backup system in the rural segments due to sizeable gap between demand and supply. The smart power distribution is estimated on the optimal outlay of the hybrid grid adopting as a smart technology and cost effective solutions of the power crisis for the emergency perusal and smart banking. To extend the gross domestic product (GDP), reliability and operational efficiency in the rural belts, the power converter based hybrid solar power system along with distributed power generation encourages for the uninterrupted power to dole out the customers as better and faster services.

articleTitle: Robust control of power system using shunt FACTS controllers
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The power demand is increasing continuously day by day. The real time power system parameters are continuously changing due to varying loading conditions, internal and external disturbances. The low frequency oscillations (LFO) are a major concern in modern stressed power system. In case if low frequency oscillations are not damped effectively, it may leads to failure of system stability and also deteriorate the power system performance. To balance the outcome of system parameters and loading uncertainties on the power system performance, robust shunt flexible AC transmission system controllers (FACTs) have been widely explored by modern power system practitioners. These controllers are able to effectively damp out the low frequency oscillations, enhance the power system stability and power flow control through the existing transmission lines. Different types of robust shunt FACTs technologies including real world installations and utility experiences have been reviewed by this paper. The comprehensive literature review show the remarkable capability of shunt FACTS controllers to get better dynamic stability voltage control and power transfer capability in the face of uncertainties present in the power system.

articleTitle: Loss allocation method independent of dynamic load variation
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The paper proposes a technique to allocate the power flow and loss in a deregulated power system. The proposed technique is developed based on the concept of relative electrical distance. An algorithm has been developed to identify the contribution of generator on the line flow and the line loss. The proposed method works with the impedance of the network, which is a fixed parameter unless there is an alterations in the network topology. This feature eliminates the requirement of repeated load flow analysis, which is used for determining generator contribution on line flow and loss by most of the existing methods. The proposed allocation method will be independent of continuous load changes in the network. Hence it can be used for determining the contribution of a generator which will be valid for longer time period unlike other commonly used power flow based methods. This method can be used to decide the cost associated with loss to the market players for a time period until new facilities are built up. Proposed technique is implemented on IEEE 30 bus system to compute the contribution of generator bus on the line loss using RED concept.

publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Provides a schedule of conference events and a listing of which papers were presented in each session.

articleTitle: Analysis of soil suitable for thermal energy storage media in renewable energy applications
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Energy storage is critically important for success of any intermittent energy source in meeting demand. Soil is used as heat transfer, heat collector and energy storage media in place of conventional used phase change materials (PCM), synthetic oils and molten salts. Thermal energy storage capacity of three soil samples such as black soil, red soil, arid/desert soil from different parts of India have been examined in terms of temperature retained with respect to time in static conditions. As soil is less costly, abundantly available and can be served as best media for thermal energy storage.

articleTitle: Model order reduction of continuous time system using hybrid metaheuristic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel method of model order reduction is presented by integrating the merits of Firefly Algorithm (FA) with Pattern Search (PS) algorithm. A linear-continuous single-input single-output system of higher order has been taken up and reduced to a lower order system. FA acts as a global optimizer while PS performs the local search in the hybrid topology to minimize the time response based error criterion. Step and frequency responses of the original and reduced systems are plotted. The superiority of the proposed method is advocated by means of a numerical example from the available literature. Further, the reduced systems are compared with some of the existing techniques in terms of Integral of Square Error (ISE). The efficacy of the proposed method is also highlighted over the existing soft computing techniques serving similar purpose.

articleTitle: MRAS based speed estimation strategies for induction motor drives: A review
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Speed sensorless induction motor drives are gaining popularity as they provide cost effective solutions with high performance delivery. Model Reference Adaptive System strategy has been extensively used for speed estimation in particular to the induction motors for developing speed sensorless drives. In this paper an exhaustive literature review on the various types of MRAS speed estimators available in the literature is presented to provide a state of art knowledge to the researchers working in this field.

articleTitle: Current harmonics reduction of three phase grid connected pulse width modulated voltage source inverter by hysteresis current controller with offset band
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The development of power electronics technology gives ample of opportunity for the grid integration of renewable in an efficient way. Commonly pulse width modulated voltage source inverter is widely used for this purpose. The control technique of grid integrated inverters plays a major role for the reduction of harmonic and improvement of power quality in the system. The most commonly used current control technique for the control of the inverter is hysteresis current controller strategies. But the main drawback hysteresis current controller is the uneven switching frequency and higher harmonic distortion. In this paper a hysteresis current controller with offset band for three phase grid integrated pulse width modulated voltage source inverter has been implemented for considerable reduction of harmonic distortion and better power quality. The MATLAB-Simulink environment is used to model, study and simulate the system.

Author Keywords: Pulse width modulated voltage source inverter (PWM VSI))

articleTitle: A single source single phase SPV grid tied system employing 9-level ternary cascaded VSC
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a single phase cascaded multilevel inverter for solar PV (SPV) grid interfaced systems. The proposed inverter consists of two H-bridge voltage source inverters (VSC) connected in cascade and are fed by a single solar photovoltaic array. Both the H-bridge VSC are connected to cascaded transformers, secondary windings of which are in ternary ratio such that 9 voltage levels are achieved. To control the proposed system, a simple decoupled current controller with an incremental conductance maximum power point tracking method is used. Both steady state and dynamic performance results in MATLAB Simulink are studied to verify the proposed system design and control algorithm.

articleTitle: Reverse recovery characteristics of the IGBT anti-parallel diode with variation in operating conditions: An experimental study
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper the focus is to study the switching characteristic of antiparallel diode in an IGBT module. The switching characteristic parameters reverse recovery time, peak reverse recovery current and corresponding energy loss during the diode turn-off transition are studied experimentally. The relationship of these characteristic parameters with the operating conditions, namely, switching voltage, device current and junction temperature is presented. This experimental study enables to decide the right diode characteristic and precise determination of device switching loss with the knowledge of IGBT switching characteristics.

articleTitle: Single stage SECS interfaced with grid using ISOGI-FLL based control algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the solar energy conversion system (SECS) tied to a three phase grid by using an improved second order generalized integrator with frequency locked loop (ISOGI-FLL) based control algorithm to mitigate the power quality problems. The steepest descent maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm is used to extract the maximum power from solar photovoltaic (SPV) array to increase the efficiency of system as well as to maintain DC link voltage of the voltage source converter (VSC). The ISOGI-FLL based control algorithm is very effective to mitigate power quality problems like harmonics, load unbalancing and poor power factor of the grid while supplying an active power to the grid. Experimental results on developed prototype have verified satisfactory operation of proposed topology for different conditions like load unbalancing, SPV (solar photovoltaic) to DSTATCOM (distribution static compensator) mode, DSTATCOM to SPV mode at variable solar insolation. Moreover, total harmonic distortions (THDs) of grid currents are found within limit of an IEEE-519 standard.

articleTitle: Impact of FACTS devices in automatic generation control of a deregulated power system
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, the impact of integration of FACTS devices viz. TCPS and TCSC on Automatic Generation Control (AGC) of a two area thermal-thermal deregulated power system have been studied in order to enhance the performance of responses such as frequency deviation and oscillation damping, deviation of tie line power between the areas and power generated by GENCOs. The comparison of results between those obtained with inclusion and exclusion FACTS devices in the system has been shown using simulations.

articleTitle: Conventional Indian railways and the advanced transportation systems: A comparative review
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents the concepts of conventional electric traction system and the advanced transportation systems adopted for research and commercialization in Indian railways. A comparative study is presented on Conventional systems, Metro transit, Pendolino trains, Talgo transit system and Maglev technologies. The principle requirements, control mechanisms, merits and demerits of electromagnetic schemes of maglev systems are also presented. Static and dynamic model explanation is given to propose the control mechanism for the development of High Speed Transit System with Maglev effect.

articleTitle: A multivariable MPPT algorithm for granular control of photovoltaic system with ripple correlation control
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A approach for the tracking of Maximum power point in Photovoltaic applications is presented in this paper. This technique can be utilized where each DC converter coupled with its own PV modules. It consists of a single controller for the utilization of multivariable MPPT based on the Ripple Correlation control. RCC utilizes the inherent ripples present in the system due to dc-dc converter consisting of power electronic switches. MATLAB simulations confirm the implementation of proposed techniques

articleTitle: A study on mitigation of blackout risks in smart grid
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The unnecessary action of critical distance relays leads to cascading failure in power system. The cascading is initial event is recognized as the main mechanism for power system blackout. Load shedding is provided for mitigate the cascading failure during the activation of critical distance relays which helps to reduce the blackout risk. The load shedding magnitude should in proper order which cannot leads to overload the transmission line. In IEEE 39 bus test system used is used for optimization of proposed algorithm which provides the continuous power transfer from generator to load without cascading failure.

articleTitle: Investigations on single-phase two winding self-excited induction generator for optimal operation with different capacitor topologies
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, the optimum operation of two winding single phase self-excited induction generator has been investigated with different capacitor topologies. The optimum values of the capacitors for different configurations are obtained using the genetic algorithm for optimum voltage regulation. The optimization is carried out under MATLAB where fsolve is used to find the magnetizing reactance and generated frequency for optimum capacitances and given prime mover speed. With such optimal values of capacitors, the performance of different configurations becomes comparable.

articleTitle: Improving the performance of PV based water pumping system for fluctuations in irradiance
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In real time field conditions, situation arises when sudden and a large change in insolation level occurs. Such frequent fluctuations in irradiation level, affects adversely the performance of Photovoltaic (PV) based water pumping system. Sudden large fall in insolation leads to generation of PV power which is insufficient for operation of motor-pump system and such frequent variations in insolation level results in unstable operation of PV based water pumping system. In this paper a standalone PV based water pumping system with super-capacitor (SC) as energy storage device is proposed. SC supports the operation of PV water pumping system in case of insolation fluctuations thus ensures stable operation of system. Proposed system is simulated in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment to verify its performance. Results show that in the designed system induction motor-pump system is able to work at constant speed, frequency despite of sudden large change in insolation.

articleTitle: Modelling and simulation of PV-Biogas based power generation system and its scopes of industrial applications: A case study on Punjab in India
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A microgrid system based on renewable energy resources is efficient, cheap and more reliable as compared to system based on single energy source. Most promising renewable energy resources such as solar and wind depend on unpredictable climate conditions. Sometimes wind is stronger whereas solar power is less or vice-versa. This paper proposes that biomass can be used as a controlled energy source which can compensate when solar energy supply is low. Integration of biomass with photovoltaic (PV) system will improve the reliability of the system. Various types of biomass can be utilized in order to generate electrical power. This paper explores the present energy scenario of Punjab in India highlighting the potential of renewable energy resources including biomass as a case study in Punjab. An approach towards integration of biomass based energy resource with solar energy based system is proposed through simulation using Matlab. The scopes of industrial applications of PV and biomass based hybrid systems are explored.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based performance analysis of three-level 48-pulse STATCOM with constant DC link voltage for reactive power compensation
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Sudden change in reactive power demand from load side leads to the voltage instability problem of the power system. This disturbance can be tackled by the proposed STATCOM (static synchronous compensator) model. It consists of four three-level VSC (voltage source converter) along with four zigzag transformers to form 48-pulse VSC. To reduce the voltage stress on the switching devices the DC link voltage is maintained constant which is not found in the common STATCOM operation. The proposed model of STATCOM is built using MATLAB/SimPowerSystems Toolbox. The performance is analyzed by switching the leading and lagging loads.

articleTitle: Estimation of average yearly power developed by a solar microgrid using Simulink model
publicationTitle: 2016 7th India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The power developed by the solar microgrid is not constant for a particular year, it depends upon the weather conditions around the year of the specific location where the solar microgrid is operating. It is however necessary to estimate the annual average power developed by the particular microgrid before physically installing microgrid at that location. The programming based model of the photovoltaic generator is developed by utilizing various governing equations of the photovoltaic cell and the microgrid model consisting of two such generators is then simulated for yearly solar insolation and temperature data of Mumbai, Bangalore, Kolkata and New Delhi. The yearly average power curves are hence obtained and their comparisons are made based upon the analysis. The above analysis helps us to estimate the rating of the loads to be connected across the microgrid.
